name: Toyota RAV4
engine: 2.5L naturally-aspirated I4 (A25A-FKS), 203 hp — 2.5L hybrid, 219 hp combined — RAV4 Prime plug-in hybrid, 302 hp combined
drivetrain: FWD or AWD (the hybrid and Prime are AWD-standard via a separate rear electric motor)
fuel_economy: 27 city / 35 hwy mpg (FWD gas) · 41 / 38 (hybrid) · 94 MPGe and ~38 mpg on gas (Prime)
reliability: 8/10 — the XA50 RAV4 rides on Toyota's proven 2.5L Dynamic Force four and hybrid system and is broadly dependable, which is a big reason it is America's best-selling non-truck. The knocks are real but manageable: early 2019 cars drew complaints about the 8-speed automatic lurching or hesitating at low speed (addressed by a TSB), some hybrids had a fuel-tank-fill issue where the tank would not fill completely, and the 2020 Denso fuel-pump recall applies. A well-sorted one is a durable, efficient family SUV.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Average · Maintenance ~$450/yr · Excellent resale — RAV4s hold value as well as anything in the segment · The hybrid's real-world ~38–40 mpg makes it the running-cost champ
popular_mods: A second set of wheels with dedicated winter or all-terrain tires — the best foul-weather/light-trail upgrade for the AWD
All-weather floor liners and a cargo liner for family and dog duty
Roof crossbars plus a cargo box or bike rack
Mild lift and A/T tires on the TRD Off-Road for the light-overlanding crowd
Honest take: the RAV4 is a practical family SUV — money is better spent on good tires, protection, and the hybrid powertrain than on chasing power

generations.4th Gen XA40 (2013–2018 US): The car-like, easygoing RAV4 — 2.5L four with a 6-speed automatic, and a first-generation hybrid from 2016. Comfortable and durable, if a bit soft and plain.
generations.5th Gen XA50 (2019–2025 US): A more rugged, TNGA-based redesign — 203 hp 2.5L four with an 8-speed automatic, a strong 219 hp hybrid, and the quick 302 hp RAV4 Prime plug-in. TRD Off-Road and Adventure trims add mild capability.
generations.6th Gen (2026+ US): The newest redesign leans further into hybrid and plug-in power; a clean XA50 remains the used-market value.

common_issues: Early 2019 8-speed automatic low-speed lurch/hesitation — a documented TSB item; test-drive at parking-lot speeds
Some 2019–2020 hybrids had a fuel-tank-fill problem (tank would not fill fully) addressed under warranty/TSB
2020 Denso low-pressure fuel-pump recall — industry-wide; confirm it is closed by VIN
More road noise than a luxury crossover, and a firmer ride on the bigger-wheeled trims
Infotainment on early XA50 cars felt dated; later years improved it
maintenance_tips: Keep up with the 0W-16 synthetic oil on the Maintenance Minder
Service the 8-speed automatic fluid on schedule — it dislikes long neglect
Confirm the fuel-pump recall and any open recalls by VIN before buying
On the hybrid, keep the traction-battery cooling intake clear and the 12V battery healthy
Rotate tires and budget for brakes on schedule; otherwise upkeep is routine Toyota
